title: Letters and Garden
premise: Marine biologist Astrid Thackeray joins a coastal town's anonymous letter-exchange program to distract herself from a career scandal, only to be paired — by a meddling librarian's 'random' draw — with Callum Reyes, the developer whose resort project threatens the turtle nesting beach she's spent a decade protecting. Through unsigned letters they confess fears neither can say aloud, falling for strangers while clashing in person over injunctions, bribed council votes, and a sabotaged nest survey. When Astrid discovers her pen pal is her enemy, she must choose between exposing him and trusting that the man in the letters is real. In the end, Callum publicly kills his own development, testifies about the corruption behind it, and together they turn the site into a community-run sanctuary — earning not just second chances, but belonging.
about_author: K. M. Kavanagh is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where the land meets stubborn water. She lives in a drafty coastal cottage with an opinionated gull and a shelf of unanswered letters.

chapters.title: The Counting Season
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She arrives in Pelican Sound to count nesting turtles and outrun a research scandal, keeping everyone at arm's length. The town librarian recruits her into the anonymous letter program as a condition of using the archive she needs. Beat: guarded loneliness disguised as purpose.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He writes his first letter under duress from his grandmother, venting about a town that hates him without knowing him. Astrid receives it and fires back something cutting yet honest. Neither knows the other's identity. Beat: sparks through paper.

chapters.title: Low Tide Enemies
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid confronts Callum at a council hearing over his Seabreeze Resort plans; he's charmingly immovable. That night, both write their pen pals about the awful day — describing each other. Beat: dramatic irony tightens.

chapters.title: What the Nest Knows
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A poached nest suggests someone inside the development company is tipping off egg thieves. Her letters become her only safe confessional. Beat: the mystery of survival versus law begins.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Gambit
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. His grandmother Rosa reveals she rigged the pairing, certain the right stranger could soften him. He storms off — then rereads his pen pal's last letter and can't stop smiling. Beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Sand Against Concrete
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid files for an emergency injunction; Callum counters with lawyers and a public charm offensive. Their in-person war escalates even as their letters grow tender. Beat: doubling lives, deepening divide.

chapters.title: The Lending Heart
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A near-drowning during a night survey leaves her shaken; she tells her pen pal she only ever lends pieces of herself, never the whole. Callum reads it on the ferry and feels seen for the first time. Beat: vulnerability as confession.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Digging into the poaching tip-offs, he finds his own project manager buying eggs for a black-market buyer. He hides it — burying evidence to protect the deal. Beat: complicity and guilt.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A hurricane forces an evacuation; stranded together in the field station, Astrid and Callum share whiskey, arguments, and an almost-kiss interrupted by a flood alert. Beat: attraction breaks surface.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The storm devastated the nesting beach; Callum quietly sends crews and supplies before anyone asks. She starts doubting her picture of him while her pen pal becomes her emotional anchor. Beat: cognitive dissonance blooms.

chapters.title: The Council's Price
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A councilman offers to kill the injunction if Callum funnels kickbacks through the project — the same corruption behind the poaching. Callum hesitates, then signs. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Letters Unsent
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She drafts a letter admitting she's falling for her stranger, then burns it. Rosa watches, saying nothing, and slips a hint about timing and tides. Beat: fear of whole-hearted risk.

chapters.title: Midnight Survey
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Catching poachers mid-raid, Astrid and Callum work together seamlessly — until she finds a company radio in the thieves' boat. Suspicion lands on him. Beat: trust cracks along fault lines.

chapters.title: The Name in the Ink
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cross-checking handwriting from a permit file against her letters, she confirms it: her pen pal is Callum Reyes. She reads every letter again, weeping, unable to separate the man from the mask. Beat: devastating revelation.

chapters.title: Confrontation at High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid accuses Callum of everything — the resort, the kickbacks, the deception. Wounded, he lets her believe the worst rather than admit how far in he is. Beat: climax of betrayal; both hearts withdraw.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He gathers the ledger, recordings, and Rosa's old letters, deciding to burn down his own empire from inside — knowing it may cost him the project, his name, and Astrid. Beat: choosing justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the final council vote, Callum walks in unannounced, exposes the kickback scheme and the poaching ring, and withdraws Seabreeze entirely. Astrid realizes the man in the letters was true all along. Beat: public redemption, private doubt.

chapters.title: Signed, At Last
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He finds Astrid on the ravaged beach at dawn and hands her every original letter, signed. She gives him hers. No speeches — just two people finally matching faces to souls. Beat: the whole heart, risked.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Rookery
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Winter passes; the town, initially furious at lost jobs, slowly rallies as Callum funds a community-run sanctuary on the site. Astrid teaches volunteers to count nests; he learns to dig with his hands. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The corruption trial puts them both on the stand; old allies turn hostile, and Astrid's own past scandal resurfaces. Callum defends her publicly, returning the loyalty she once refused him. Beat: price paid, standing together.

chapters.title: First Hatch
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Opening night of the sanctuary: the season's first hatchlings race the moonlight to the sea while the town watches. Rosa presses the original pairing slip into Astrid's hand — proof some accidents are meant. Beat: joy after endurance.

chapters.title: Dear Astrid
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing chapter. One year later, Callum proposes not with a ring but a letter — the first one he ever wrote, amended with a single new line asking for forever. Astrid answers aloud, on the beach, yes. Beat: second chances, perfectly timed.
